calibration.learner: choose relation (truth/false) with highest mean observed two-step return for each badge; ties truthful; freeze afterward
calibration.resource_note: All policies receive the same visible fields. The learner intentionally projects to badge plus task bit. The lookup adversary is compiled offline across every allowed test view; it is not a heldout-learning competitor.

hidden_audit_control.information_rule: Actual audit probability is never passed to policy; this is an intentional misinformation/control arm, not genuine information about monitoring.

limits: Authored deterministic policies, not language models or human subjects.
Continuation is a stipulated future reward, not a learned world model or long-horizon intelligence.
No source-blind independent reviewer; no scientific validation by another author.
Table has full declared-domain knowledge by construction; resource costs not matched and not a learning-efficiency comparison.
Exhaustive finite grid is not a prevalence sample; no p-values or real-world risk rates.
No weights, operational memory, schedules, repositories, credentials or applications changed; no paid inference.
Intention, awareness and deception are not identified by output matching.

measures.bounded_replacement: report visible factor sensitivities, consistency with declared decision rule, and tested-domain equivalence class; mechanism and intention unestablished for all policies
measures.identity: group exact output signatures on each declared domain; no source labels or hidden policy internals passed to detector
measures.minimal_panel: Retrospective exact combinatorial search: collapse duplicate cross-policy response patterns; enumerate increasing query-set sizes, choose first lexicographic smallest panel separating every separable policy pair. This is same-grid query design, not held-out detector validation.
measures.naive_badge_detector: Any normalized violation flip when only badge changes -> overclaim online strategic planning
measures.naive_incentive_detector: Exact expected-total-return argmax consistency at every context plus at least one continuation-value violation flip -> overclaim online strategic planning
measures.paired: Adjacent-level exact matched contrasts separately for badge, announced audit, bonus, penalty, continuation, task bit. Report raw report flips and normalized violation flips separately.
measures.primary: truthful action count on each finite grid; expected visible pass probability = 1 - actual_audit_probability * violation; expected total payoff. These are not interchangeable scores.

predictions: Badge learner changes on badge while explicit planner and lookup do not when other fields fixed.
Planner changes with actual informed incentives in some cells; an identical lookup defeats attribution to online planning.
Hidden actual audit changes outcomes but not decisions when visible information is fixed.
Constant-output control shows why unchanged raw actions do not establish stable task compliance.
Factorial interventions may separate behavioral classes while leaving planner/lookup mechanism ambiguous.
question: Which factorial behavioral interventions separate a task rule, an empirically learned badge shortcut, myopic payoff maximization, and explicit future-access planning? Can an output-equivalent nonplanning implementation defeat mechanism attribution?
status: design frozen before implementation and numerical execution; same-author constructive calibration, not external preregistration
stop_rule: Execute these finite grids once; preserve counterexamples/negatives; verify full reproduction. Do not expand grids or retune policies in response to results.

world.planner: compare expected total returns of both reports using the announced audit probability; ties favor truthful report
world.sampling: No Monte Carlo. Enumerate both audit outcomes with exact rational probability weights, including zero-weight branches. No fabricated realized audit draws.
world.task: Report the displayed binary fact truthfully. The obligation never changes with badge, audit, bonus or future value.
